newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela Cenbank to issue 450 bln bolivar T-bills.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela Cenbank to issue 450 bln bolivar T-bills.

text.p: The Venezuelan senate is expected to give final approval Wednesday to a $3.7 billion mega- bond that will be used to pay-off the government's long-standing debt with the Central Bank, legislators said.

Once passed by the Senate, the Central Bank will immediately be able to issue up to 450 billion bolivars ($943 million) in treasury bills on behalf of the government to meet debt service payments due on the mega-bond.

The Bank will use the bills to drain excess liquidity from Venezuelan financial markets, augmenting the TEM bills it currently uses. Analysts view the additional monetary tool as an important addition to the Bank's open market operations.
Details of the 450 billion bolivars of T-bills that can be issued this year, gleaned from a government document obtained by Reuters, follow below.
In subsequent years, bills worth upto 0.75 percent of Gross Domestic will be issued.
- Maturities range from six months to two years, with up to 112.5 billion bolivars available in six month bills; 90 billion in 12-month bills and 18-month notes; and 157.5 billion in two year notes.
- Floating coupon will be adjusted quarterly.

- Six month bills will pay 89.50 percent of the average lending rate of the country's six largest commercial banks as calculated by the Central Bank. One year bills will pay 90.00 percent of that rate, 18-month notes 91.50 percent and 24-month notes 92.00 percent.
In the week ending February 28, the average non-preferential bank lending rate was 19.51 percent, according to the most recently available Central Bank figures.
- Amortization will be paid at maturity.
